summary:
Space Mission Design Game is an interactive educational experience that turns the complex process of planning a space mission into an engaging, hands-on challenge. Players design and manage a complete mission—from defining scientific objectives to building a spacecraft, selecting a launch vehicle, planning an orbit, and simulating mission operations.
The game highlights the real-world trade-offs faced by aerospace engineers: adding a powerful science instrument may improve scientific value, but it also increases mass, power demand, data volume, and cost. Players must balance these competing constraints while staying within budget, launch capacity, power limits, communication capabilities, and mission duration. This mirrors how real mission teams prioritize requirements and make sacrifices to achieve the best possible science return.

For students who may never get to design an entire spacecraft from concept to operation, the game makes abstract engineering trade-offs tangible. It encourages systems thinking, collaboration, problem-solving, and evidence-based decision-making—skills central to real aerospace mission design. NASA’s educational mission-design activities similarly ask students to balance science goals with mass, power, budget, and launch constraints.
details:
Define a mission objective and select science requirements.

Design the spacecraft structure, payload, and subsystems.

Choose scientific instruments, power systems, communications, and onboard computing.

Select a launch vehicle, trajectory, and orbit.

Manage limited resources such as budget, mass, power, data, and communications.

Run mission reviews, tests, launch, operations, and end-of-mission evaluation.

See how every design decision affects the mission’s overall success
